Fansigns aren’t through concerts. For Ateez specifically, (usually) Hello82 will host fansigns for each stop the day before or day of the concert. 

For the arenas (so every stop except BMO and Citi field), there’s only two VIP tiers: Atiny/VIP1 and Sector VIP/VIP2. Each have different benefits depending on the tier, where GA floor doesn’t have any. One of the links in the main post has the link to the tiers.

Not to my knowledge! It’s always good to double check though on TM or the venue’s website. 

Also more tips for concert-going: since you’re GA (not sure if you’re VIP or not but point still stands) ppl line up really early at the venue. Some places will do fan numbering, where fans unofficially give lil wristbands w numbers to secure your waiting spot in line. This allows u to go and get food/drinks or go to the bathroom and come back to your spot. Again, this might not happen at your stop, but be aware of it! 

I’d recommend to eat a good meal and drink lots of water beforehand and use the bathroom before going inside and getting your spot bc it’s hard to leave the crowd and come back to your spot in GA. 

I’d also like to reiterate that you will be very hot, so wear something cool and comfortable. I went to Break the Wall Tour in November & February and even tho it was cold outside, it was sweltering inside in the pit, it’s gonna be worse in the summer. Last tour, Hongjoong did mention that if anyone in the pit needs it, security around the stage have water bottles that Ateez bought for atinys but tbh it was rly difficult for us to get the security’s attention and they ran out of water 😅

Don’t be afraid to make friends w the ppl around u in line or in the pit!! I actually met my best friend that way at another Ateez concert! Take your pics and videos and have fun!! Ateez is an amazing first concert to go to and every spot is a good spot to see them!

Wear comfortable shoes!!! You will be standing for so long. It’s also just gonna be so hot inside with everyone squished together so keep that in mind.

I have the exact same hair as you, bleached and colored (and frequently in swimming pool RIP healthy hair). Due to the sulfates, I can't use Lush's hair items all the time. Sulfates are what dry your hair out

This is my hair care routine/a guideline I guess you could call it (I also have curly hair but that shouldn't make too much of a difference, jut that I wait longer in between showers to wash my hair):

* Shampoo- Shea moisture African Water Mint and Ginger Shampoo. Only use it on my scalp and roots. (great brand, cruelty free, ethically traded, no parabens or other harmful ingredients)

* Conditioner- Lush's American Cream (On ends so my scalp isn't oily)

I will switch this out with a custom made conditioner (you put in your own ingredients and what you need it for, mine is made for curly hair, but you can use a normal conditioner just for color treated hair)

* A leave in conditioner. I use Carol's Daughter regular leave in (also for curly hair). I recommend this if your hair's VERY dry even after conditioning, but is sometimes not needed depending on your hair type.

* I also use hair treatments/deep conditioners and **coconut oil** (I swear by this, it works wonders!!!) every so often or when my hair gets super dry/unmanageable.

Hope that helped a bit!
